<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תמוז_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919103_theRebbe_196" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_9E_D7_95_D7_96_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919103_theRebbe_196__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Korach's dispute and his challenge to Aharon are interconnected, rooted in the attribute of Gevurah which gives rise to division.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And one may add,</t>
    <t s="1">that these two matters in "and Korach took"</t>
    <t s="2">(the dispute,</t>
    <t s="3">and that he disputed against Aharon)</t>
    <t s="4">are related to each other.</t>
    <t s="5">For, behold, the creation of the dispute</t>
    <t s="6">(the firmament that separates)</t>
    <t s="7">was specifically on the second day,</t>
    <t s="8">because the first day is the attribute of Chessed</t>
    <t s="9">(right),</t>
    <t s="10">and the second day is the attribute of Gevurah</t>
    <t s="11">(left),</t>
    <t s="12">and from the side of Gevurah there is a granting of place for dispute.</t>
    <t s="13">And as it is brought in the Zohar there: "The right is the perfection of all... in it depends all perfection,</t>
    <t s="14">when the left is aroused, dispute is aroused."</t>
    <t s="15">And based on this, it can be said,</t>
    <t s="16">that the essential matter of Korach is dispute</t>
    <t s="17">[as is also understood from that which our sages said,</t>
    <t s="18">"Whoever holds onto a dispute transgresses a negative commandment,</t>
    <t s="19">as it is said,</t>
    <t s="20">'And you shall not be like Korach and his assembly,'</t>
    <t s="21">for from this that one who holds onto a dispute</t>
    <t s="22">(whatever dispute it may be)</t>
    <t s="23">is like Korach and his assembly,</t>
    <t s="24">it is proven</t>
    <t s="25">that the essential matter of Korach is dispute],</t>
    <t s="26">and that he disputed against Aharon</t>
    <t s="27">(Chessed)</t>
    <t s="28">and wanted to make the Gevuros primary,</t>
    <t s="29">this was in order that through this there would be strengthening for the dispute.</t>
    <t s="30">And it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="31">Korach was clever,</t>
    <t s="32">and it is reasonable to say that his dispute against Aharon's priesthood was because he erred in the ways of service,</t>
    <t s="33">and it is not understood,</t>
    <t s="34">why did he desire dispute.</t>
    <t s="35">For this, that he disputed against Aharon,</t>
    <t s="36">can be explained,</t>
    <t s="37">that Korach thought that the service of G-d should be in the line of Gevurah,</t>
    <t s="38">and therefore he disputed against Aharon whose service was in the line of Chessed.</t>
    <t s="39">But according to what was said above, that Korach wanting to make the Gevuros primary was in order to strengthen the dispute,</t>
    <t s="40">it is not understood,</t>
    <t s="41">how did Korach think that dispute is a path in the service of G-d.</t>
    <t s="42">And also it needs to be understood what the Targum translates "and Korach took" [as "and Korach separated"],</t>
    <t s="43">for "and he separated" is like the firmament that separates,</t>
    <t s="44">for ostensibly,</t>
    <t s="45">behold, even the name of Korach himself hints at the firmament that separates,</t>
    <t s="46">as the Tzemach Tzedek said on the verse "And Korach took"</t>
    <t s="47">that Korach hints at the firmament that separates, as it is said,</t>
    <t s="48">"a firmament like the appearance of the ice [kerach],"</t>
    <t s="49">and what is the addition of "and Korach separated."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The firmament separating upper and lower waters represents the partition between spiritual and physical pleasures, enabling the lower waters to ascend higher through their yearning.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood by prefacing the known matter regarding the firmament that separates between water and water,</t>
    <t s="2">that waters are delight,</t>
    <t s="3">for that water causes all kinds of delight to grow</t>
    <t s="4">is because in them is the aspect of delight.</t>
    <t s="5">And the firmament that separates between the upper waters and the lower waters is the partition through which the separation is made between the delights in spiritual matters</t>
    <t s="6">(upper waters)</t>
    <t s="7">and the delights of this world</t>
    <t s="8">(lower waters).</t>
    <t s="9">And the intention of the firmament separating between upper waters and lower waters is in order that through this the lower waters will ascend higher than they were before their descent.</t>
    <t s="10">For through their descent below,</t>
    <t s="11">there is generated in them the desire and thirst to ascend above,</t>
    <t s="12">"the lower waters weep, saying, 'We desire to be before the King,'"</t>
    <t s="13">and through this they ascend higher than they were before their descent,</t>
    <t s="14">and higher even than the upper waters.</t>
    <t s="15">And this is what our sages said,</t>
    <t s="16">that on the third day "it is good" is said twice—one for the work of the waters and one for the work of the day,</t>
    <t s="17">for ostensibly,</t>
    <t s="18">behold, the work of the waters is a matter of dispute, and how can "it is good" be said about it?</t>
    <t s="19">And the explanation of this is,</t>
    <t s="20">that through the service of man, the clarification and ascent of the lower waters is accomplished,</t>
    <t s="21">and therefore,</t>
    <t s="22">on the third day, when "the waters were gathered from under the heavens to one place and the dry land appeared,"</t>
    <t s="23">and dry land is the place of man,</t>
    <t s="24">the intention of the work of the waters was completed,</t>
    <t s="25">that through the separation of the lower waters from the upper waters and their descent below, they ascend higher than they were before their descent,</t>
    <t s="26">and then</t>
    <t s="27">(after the possibility of this ascent is made),</t>
    <t s="28">even the work of the waters is good.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Korach mistakenly thought the purpose of the lower waters' descent was to reveal the superiority of physicality itself, leading him to prioritize Gevurah and dispute, but the true revelation of the lower waters' root will only occur in the future.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And based on this, it will be understood why Korach desired dispute,</t>
    <t s="2">for Korach thought that the intention in this, that the lower waters were separated from the upper waters and descended below, was for the sake of the superiority that exists in the physical delights themselves,</t>
    <t s="3">that the root of physicality is higher than the root of spirituality.</t>
    <t s="4">[And in the manner explained in Torah Ohr,</t>
    <t s="5">that in the upper worlds it is said,</t>
    <t s="6">"How great are Your works,"</t>
    <t s="7">and the matter of "how many are Your works"</t>
    <t s="8">is specifically in the lower worlds,</t>
    <t s="9">and the matter of multiplicity indicates the perfection of Ein Sof,</t>
    <t s="10">that despite His being singular,</t>
    <t s="11">He also bears a multiplicity of details.]</t>
    <t s="12">And therefore he wanted the Gevuros to be primary,</t>
    <t s="13">because this that "the lower waters weep, saying, 'We desire to be before the King'" is because the superiority of the matter of revelations is felt in them</t>
    <t s="14">(Chessed,</t>
    <t s="15">right),</t>
    <t s="16">and since the revelations are primarily in the upper worlds,</t>
    <t s="17">therefore the lower waters</t>
    <t s="18">(in which there are no revelations)</t>
    <t s="19">want to leave their existence and ascend above.</t>
    <t s="20">But according to Korach's error, that the intention is in the physical delights themselves,</t>
    <t s="21">that their physical root should be revealed,</t>
    <t s="22">behold, on the contrary,</t>
    <t s="23">the primary superiority is in the tzimtzumim and Gevuros,</t>
    <t s="24">from which physical things are generated.</t>
    <t s="25">But Korach erred in this,</t>
    <t s="26">for the revelation of the root of the lower waters</t>
    <t s="27">(physical)</t>
    <t s="28">themselves will be in the future,</t>
    <t s="29">and in order for there to be a revelation of the root of the lower waters themselves,</t>
    <t s="30">there must first be in them the feeling of the superiority of revelations,</t>
    <t s="31">that through this feeling there is in them the thirst and desire to ascend above,</t>
    <t s="32">and through this there will be a revelation of the root of the lower waters themselves.</t>
    <t s="33">And this is why "it is good" was not said regarding the work of the waters until the third day,</t>
    <t s="34">even though there is also a superiority in the work of the waters as it was on the second day,</t>
    <t s="35">in that the lower waters were separated from the upper waters and descended below,</t>
    <t s="36">because the revelation of this superiority will only be in the future,</t>
    <t s="37">and now,</t>
    <t s="38">the intention of the descent of the waters below is in order that they will ascend above</t>
    <t s="39">(as above),</t>
    <t s="40">and this matter is accomplished specifically on the third day.</t>
    <t s="41">And likewise is it regarding the general matter of revelation</t>
    <t s="42">(the root of Chessed)</t>
    <t s="43">and tzimtzum</t>
    <t s="44">(the root of Gevurah),</t>
    <t s="45">that the superiority in the tzimtzum itself will only be revealed in the future,</t>
    <t s="46">and the intention of the tzimtzum as it is now is for the sake of revelation.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
